correctness.rationale: Every selected set is uniquely A union F. Omitting B forces all inserted edges internal to B; semitotal witness conditions reduce to a crossing choice only in the b=1, b=2 or a=1 cases. Distances are checked explicitly, giving a necessary/sufficient complete classification. The sum follows by independent free-edge choices. The coefficient minimization handles n=3 and n=4 boundaries. Direct exhaustive adjacency verification for n=3..6 matches each coefficient.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The claimed conclusion is a generating polynomial counting every semitotal dominating subset by size, plus coefficients at the minimum. Knowing only the minimum semitotal domination number or the ordinary domination polynomial does not imply this refined count. Ordinary dominating sets may fail the semitotal witness condition; in S(K_3)=C_6 a two-vertex opposite dominating set fails because its chosen vertices have distance three.

value.rationale: The complete cardinality distribution and exact count of minimum solutions give a natural nontrivial refinement of a known extremal invariant on a canonical subdivision graph; the all-weight classification separates ordinary domination from semitotal witness feasibility, and isolates the nonempty-cross-edge obstruction and exceptional four-original-vertex minimum count.
